summary:
THE RULING STANDS AND THE TWO REPAIRS STAND. FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0 is refused by name at the first conversion that reads it, before any Config is frozen; every neighbouring legal value builds, the shipped default first; the filed edit really would have broken tests/test_derive.py:407 and the 'is zero' repair really does keep it green; every configuration the report quotes reproduces line for line, and all twelve path::symbol citations plus all six self_organize.py line citations resolve to the right thing. Suite re-run at HEAD: ownership 15+70, contract 16+77, census 8, assemble 9, couplings 4, fabric 9, derive 575/0 -- green, and correctly green.

SEVEN THINGS THEY DID NOT REPORT, THREE OF THEM THE UNTRIPPABLE-GUARD SHAPE THE BRIEF ASKED FOR.
1. F8's PER-LAYER REPORT IS A HARDCODED STRING (high). The report leans on it twice as the honest substitute for an assertion it cannot make -- 'it prints the truth every run'. It prints a literal. I moved FAB.d_manage_period's compute off flush_period_windows onto its Steps twin on a copy of the tree: F8 PASSES, 9 checks 0 failing, and still names flush_period_windows while the refusal came from flush_period. That move is the second of the four things src/fabric/api.py names as 'WHAT WOULD MAKE IT FIRE AGAIN'. One line fixes it.
2. flush_period's ZERO ARM IS UNTRIPPABLE. Reverting it to `< 0` leaves all seven suite files green while flush_period(Steps(0), 16) answers Flushes(1). The report says it 'changes nothing reachable'; it does not say no check can see it. tests/test_derive.py already makes exactly this complaint about the four NEGATIVE arms and closes it with an assertion.
3. 'is zero' IS ASSERTED BY NOTHING. Collapsing both arms back to an unconditional 'is negative' -- the wording the filed edit was REFUTED for -- leaves the whole suite green. The repair is as unprotected as the defect.
4-5. THE CAP HALF, WHICH THE BRIEF CALLED THE IMPORTANT ONE. 'Nothing distinguishable is removed today' is TRUE today -- I confirmed both legs, and the identity of 0 and 1 is algebraic at every batch width, not just the default. It does NOT survive observe: pin_tick clamps at zero, so held == Windows(0) is a state the written arithmetic reaches at every start-of-run and every re-pin, and there `held >= 0` is True while `held >= 1` is False. And the enforcement is worse than latent -- it rests entirely on two wires capacity/api.py and spine/assemble.py both declare REPORTING-ONLY and docs/04_CONTRACT.md::Q-CLOCK-1 has already specified the atomic edit that DELETES. I applied that edit: CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=0 builds again, and so does -20000, taking the 2026-09-05 negative refusal with it. spine/derive.py::pin_tick already carries the Q-CLOCK-1 warning; the new CAP paragraph 700 lines above it does not.
6. AN OVERSTATEMENT AT THE HEART OF THE ARGUMENT. derive.py says DOM 'DECLARED the sentinel and GUARDED IT AT ITS OWN READ SITE'. The citation resolves to a P4 stub, and DOM's one LIVE read site says in its own words that the guard 'is not implemented anywhere yet'. Measured: DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=0 builds and hands a reader Windows(0). So after this change the lever that declares NOTHING for 0 is refused and the lever that declares 0 to mean NEVER is not -- the split runs the other way from the argument. O13 cannot see this: the symbol exists, it just does not support the sentence.
7. Finding 6 pastes '(no hit)' for a grep that prints three lines (the claim is right, the paste is not), and src/fabric/api.py's 'it still reaches the same readers it reaches today' was falsified by this change and left standing.

NOTHING HERE MAKES ANY LEVER SAFE, BOUNDED OR VALIDATED, and the report does not claim it does: FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=1 and every value above it remain legal and unbounded at the top, and I found no forbidden word and no ceiling claim in the 130 added lines.

findings.item: THE CAP HALF: 'nothing distinguishable is removed today' is TRUE today

(1) 0 and 1 build identical wires, and not only at the default rate -- the identity is algebraic. For every legal batch_windows w >= 1: 0//w == 0 and 1//w is 0 (w>1) or 1 (w==1), and the OUTPUT floor sends 0 to Flushes(1), so both spell Flushes(1) at every w. CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=2 is the first distinguishable value at w==1.
(2) No executable body in src/ reads cap.pin_windows. capacity/api.py::observe and ::counters both end in NotImplementedError; new_valve does not read it (its guard is `float(cap.lift) < 0 or int(cap.lift_min) < 0`). findings.item: ...and it does NOT survive observe being written: CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=0 becomes distinguishable the moment the stub lands
findings.detail:
The brief asked exactly this and the answer is no. capacity/api.py::observe's FROZEN contract makes pin_windows a threshold on an accumulated clock -- 'pinned: ... accumulated by derive.pin_tick and DECAYED while below' -- and declares the block reason `threshold(held/pin_windows)`. derive.pin_tick IS written, and it CLAMPS AT ZERO on the way down ('an unpinned population that has been unpinned longer than it was pinned does not owe the valve negative time'). So held == Windows(0) is a state the written arithmetic reaches -- at the start of every run, and again after any decay -- and at that state `held >= Windows(0)` is True while `held >= Windows(1)` is False.
THAT IS THE DISTINCTION THE REPORT SAYS DOES NOT EXIST. CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=0 is 'a lift is earned the instant the population pins' -- the sweep's own words for it -- and CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=1 is 'a lift is earned one accumulated window later'. They differ on the first pinned flush of a run and on every re-pin after a decay to zero. So this is a latent refusal of a coherent CAP configuration, filed under FAB's name, and the report's own sentence -- 'this arm is then the thing to revisit' -- is the only thing that will remember it, in a docstring, in another package's file.
WHAT THE REPORT DID GET RIGHT AND I AM NOT TAKING AWAY: it named the collateral rather than letting it land silently, it drove it, it printed it in F8 every run, and it explicitly declined to rule that 0 is meaningless for a threshold. The defect is that 'nothing distinguishable is removed today' is stated as the ANSWER when it is only true of today, and today is defined by two stubs.

findings.item: AND THE WHOLE REFUSAL OF CAP_PIN_WINDOWS<1 RESTS ON TWO WIRES docs/04_CONTRACT.md HAS ALREADY WRITTEN THE ATOMIC EDIT TO DELETE
findings.detail:
Unreported, and it is the other half of the same problem. The only path by which CAP_PIN_WINDOWS reaches flush_period_windows is FAB.d_cap_lift_period and TOK.d_cap_lift_period, and BOTH are declared REPORTING-ONLY: capacity/api.py's module docstring says 'Those rows survive in this contract as REPORTING wires only (see FOR THE OWNER Q-CLOCK-1); the valve does not read either of them', and spine/assemble.py's own row reason says 'This row is REPORTING'. docs/04_CONTRACT.md::Q-CLOCK-1 is MEASURABLE, not settled: it specifies option (b) in full -- 'delete both Coupling rows, both WIRES READ lines, both `_ =` reads, the paragraph in TOK.lift_vocab_cap, and the two wire names inside derive.pin_tick's UnitError message -- one atomic edit across ~8 files' -- and names the condition that triggers it: CAP.counters getting a body whose block-reason histogram distinguishes 'never full' from 'never plateaued'.
SO THE TWO P4 DELIVERABLES PULL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND EITHER ORDER IS WRONG. If observe lands first, a coherent CAP configuration is refused at build under a cadence argument. If Q-CLOCK-1 (b) lands first, the refusal EVAPORATES with nothing saying so -- and it takes the NEGATIVE refusal with it, which is not this change's but is a live defect fix from 2026-09-05. I measured that: with the two rows retired exactly as Q-CLOCK-1 specifies, CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=0 AND CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-20000 both build again.
THE FILE ALREADY KNOWS HOW TO SAY THIS AND THIS DOCSTRING DOES NOT. spine/derive.py::pin_tick, 700 lines below, carries exactly the warning: 'THE REPORTING WIRES ARE NOT PERMANENT: Q-CLOCK-1 is MEASURABLE, and the condition that retires both rows ... is written out there.' flush_period_windows' new CAP paragraph -- the one that argues the collateral -- never mentions Q-CLOCK-1, and it is the paragraph a reader arriving at the refusal reads.
THE EDIT: one sentence in flush_period_windows' CAP paragraph, pointing at Q-CLOCK-1 the way pin_tick already does, and saying that this arm is CAP's only refusal of a sub-one pin threshold and goes with those rows. It asserts nothing new and weakens nothing.

findings.item: OVERSTATEMENT: derive.py says DOM 'DECLARED the sentinel and GUARDED IT AT ITS OWN READ SITE'. DOM's read site says the guard is not implemented, and DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=0 builds
findings.detail:
src/spine/derive.py:400-410 (and the same claim in the refusal message and in .rework/audits/d_manage.json's summary point 1) makes DOM the precedent for refusing FAB's zero: 'DOM then DECLARED 0 to mean NEVER and guarded it at its own read site (domains/api.py::manage)'. The citation resolves -- the quoted sentence is really at src/domains/api.py:333-334 -- but the symbol it resolves to is a P4 STUB that ends in NotImplementedError, so the quoted text is a CONTRACT for an unwritten body, not a guard.
DOM'S ONE LIVE READ SITE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS. src/domains/api.py::manage_period: 'ZERO IS NOT TOUCHED ... src/domains/levers.py carries a PORT REQUIREMENT that 0 must mean NEVER behind a guard at the read site, AND IT IS NOT IMPLEMENTED ANYWHERE YET ... The test below is strictly `< 0`.' Measured: DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=0 builds, DOM.manage_period hands back Windows(0), and cadences_that_cannot_fire reports ('dom.manage', 0, 0).
THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE ONE ARGUED. After this change the lever that declares NOTHING for 0 (FAB_MANAGE_EVERY) is refused at build, while the lever that DECLARES 0 to mean NEVER (DOM_MANAGE_EVERY) accepts it and hands it to a reader. The split the whole argument rests on now runs the other way, and the two levers were split from one knob. This is O13's blind spot exactly: a citation that resolves to an existing symbol which does not support the sentence built on it.
THE EDIT, in derive.py, and it costs the ruling nothing: replace 'guarded it at its own read site' with what is true -- 'DECLARED the sentinel in domains/api.py::manage's frozen contract and recorded the guard as a PORT REQUIREMENT that domains/api.py::manage_period says is not implemented yet; FAB declared nothing at all'. The asymmetry that carries the ruling (a DECLARATION exists for DOM and none for FAB) survives verbatim.

findings.item: THE THREE-ANSWER ARGUMENT IS REALLY A TWO-ANSWER ONE: the third 'answer' is a declared sentinel report from the same file
findings.detail:
The ruling holds, but one third of its stated evidence is not a contradictory reading. The report and the docstring both count spine/derive.py::cadences_that_cannot_fire returning ('fab.manage', 0, 0) as a third live reader saying 'this gate CANNOT FIRE'. That function's own body comment, 200 lines below the new refusal in the SAME file, says the opposite about that row: 'A PERIOD OF ZERO OR LESS IS A SENTINEL, AND IT MUST BE REPORTED, NOT SKIPPED ... It is reported with run_windows as 0 to say "this is not a length comparison". ckpt/api.py states what the sentinel means there -- "every == 0 means the only save is the final one plus SIGUSR1" -- which is a LEGITIMATE configuration and exactly the kind of thing the report must SAY.'
CKPT_EVERY's shipped DEFAULT is 0 and it is a live declared sentinel, so this exact row shape is printed for a legitimate configuration on every default run. A (key, 0, 0) row therefore means 'a zero period was declared here, go read what it means', not 'this gate cannot fire'.
WHAT SURVIVES INTACT, and it is enough for the ruling: the genuine contradiction is two readers, not three -- the FAB.d_manage_period wire spelling Flushes(1) ('manage on EVERY flush') against FAB.manage_period spelling Windows(0). That is a real opposite-sentence pair over one number with no declaration behind it, and it carries the refusal on its own. DEFERRED rather than REFUTED for that reason.

findings.item: DID A RETIREMENT LOSE A VALUE / DID A DOMAIN BREAK A SENTINEL / WAS A BOUND DERIVED FROM U.FRACTION
findings.detail:
Three of the brief's questions come back clean on this change, and it is worth saying why so the next round does not re-drive them.
NO RETIREMENT. Nothing was retired here. The old clause was `n < 0` and the new one is `n < 1`, which strictly CONTAINS it, so every value the old clause refused is still refused. I drove the OLD clause's boundary rather than the new one: -1, -5, -1000, -20000 and -1e-320 (which coerce refuses one layer earlier, by name) on both levers, and every one still refuses with 'is negative' in the message. Nothing slipped through the gap.
NO DOMAIN, SO NO SENTINEL BROKEN BY ONE. This change declared no domain= on any lever; it is a read-site refusal. The only sentinel question it raises is CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=0, filed above as latent rather than live. The tree's two nearby LIVE zero sentinels are untouched and I checked both: CKPT_EVERY=0 (the shipped DEFAULT, 'the only save is the final one plus SIGUSR1') and MEM_REKEY_EVERY=0 ('0 DISARMS', memory/api.py::maintain) are neither of them routed through flush_period_windows -- exactly three COUPLINGS rows call it, at spine/assemble.py:787, :807 and :837, carrying FAB_MANAGE_EVERY and CAP_PIN_WINDOWS and nothing else.
NO U.FRACTION ARGUMENT ANYWHERE IN IT. The refusal argues from what the READER does with the number -- a windows/flushes conversion and the floor beneath it -- and never from a unit label. The lever is U.Windows and the argument is about the conversion, which is the right side of the tree's three previous rulings on this.

findings.item: THE SHAPE O15 CANNOT SEE, which this change is an instance of
findings.detail:
Answering the brief's question 6 rather than reporting a defect. O15's own CANNOT CATCH list rules this refusal out by construction: 'a refusal written anywhere but an `if` over a Config-annotated parameter with a literal `owned_by`'. flush_period_windows' arm is an `if` over a units.Windows ARGUMENT, in the spine, in a file with no Config and no owned_by, so it is not in O15's population at all -- not abstained on, absent.
THE SHAPE IS: A CROSS-PACKAGE RANGE REFUSAL LIVING IN THE SPINE. It binds levers of two packages at build time (FAB_MANAGE_EVERY and CAP_PIN_WINDOWS), through a coupling table, with no declaration on either lever to compare it against and no package body that could contradict it. Neither O15, nor the census, nor the contract checks can pair it with anything. F8 is the only check that drives it, only for FAB's lever, and only REPORTS the CAP half. That is why the two CAP findings above had to be found by reading the coupling table rather than by any check going red, and it is where the next such refusal will hide.
